About half of the tickets for "Double The Money" have been sold. The game is in the middle of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

The numbers for "Double The Money" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2415.headline: Tickets sold so far

2416.body:
"Loaded with $2,000s" has 63,206 prizes of $20 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $500 prize, with 1,045 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Every line of Loaded with $2,000s's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2416.headline: The prize table, line by line

2419.body:
"Bronze 7s" has 107,880 prizes of $1 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $250 prize, with fourteen left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Everything above about "Bronze 7s" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2419.headline: What's actually left to win

2420.body:
"Silver 7s" has gone over a month without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $177,777 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything above about "Silver 7s" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2420.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

Today's free summary of "Gold 7s" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2421.headline: A close look at the prizes

2422.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Platinum 7s", about half are still unsold. The game is near the midpoint of its run, with two of three top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The numbers for "Platinum 7s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.

2427.headline: What's actually left to win

2428.body:
"PEPPERMINT PAYOUT" has five of five top prizes left and is near the start of its run. About a quarter of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Tomorrow's count on "PEPPERMINT PAYOUT" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
2428.headline: How much has sold

2429.body:
"MERRY MONEY TREE" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $125,000 was claimed earlier this week. Unsold tickets still hold three of the original four. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

If you play "MERRY MONEY TREE" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2429.headline: A player won a top prize

2430.body:
"WRAPPED IN RICHES" offers a top prize of $500,000 and ten prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward the smaller prizes. Games shaped like this pay out often, in small amounts. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

Every line of WRAPPED IN RICHES's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
